overview: This is a "rule," a House resolution that sets the terms for debating other legislation. It sets up votes on two resolutions that would cancel rules from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the federal agency that oversees consumer financial products: one on overdraft fees at very large banks, and one bringing big digital payment apps under the agency's supervision. It also sets up debate on H.R. 1526, which would limit federal district courts' power to issue court orders (injunctions) that block government actions, and H.R. 22, which would require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections. Each measure gets one hour of debate with limited amendment opportunities. The resolution also adopts House Resolution 293 on announcing vote pairs and sets aside (tables) House Resolution 164. The House adopted it on April 8, 2025.
for: Supporters say the rule moves several priority measures to a floor vote efficiently, with set debate time, and resolves a dispute over how absent members can register their positions.
against: Critics say it bundles unrelated, significant bills under tight debate limits with few chances to amend them, and uses the rule to set aside a separate pending resolution without a direct vote on it.
